Contract.title: A fourth skill, grace5-orchestrate, runs several approved changes in one mostly unattended session, and every skill reads a repository's optional local extensions
Contract.Problem: Explicit owner requirement of 2026-11-13: GRACE 5 must ship, out of the box, the counterpart of the GRACE 4 batch orchestrator, which was bound to GRACE 4 and to one project and cannot be reused. Today the three skills carry one change each; running several in a row, unattended, with the owner asked only what is critical, is left to each session's improvisation. A repository also has no place to tell every GRACE 5 role once how it works locally, for example which issue tracker receives discoveries or how an implementer is launched.
Contract.Change: Local extensions. A repository may keep prose instruction files in .grace5/extensions/, one topic per file, each saying in its own words which roles it addresses. The folder is optional; the kernel never creates, reads, writes or validates it. Each of the four skills says, in one sentence, that its reader reads the files there before working and follows those addressed to its role, and method.md defines the folder in one section. An extension may replace a skill's default and may grant standing authority for outward-facing actions; it cannot grant, and no skill takes from it, an owner gate the kernel reserves. The orchestrated run. A fourth skill, skills/grace5-orchestrate, defines it. One orchestrating session takes the open changes that status reports as approved for execution, lists every other open change as left out with the reason, and carries each taken change from start to close through subagents: an implementer that follows grace5-execute and an independent reviewer that follows grace5-review. The orchestrator implements nothing itself, reads the state of a change from grace5 status and never from a subagent's report, runs grace5 close, and keeps a run ledger on disk from which a fresh session can resume. By default changes run one at a time in the current worktree, in id order, each closed or parked before the next starts; concurrency and isolated workspaces exist only where an extension provides and authorizes them. The owner is asked only about a critical stop, and the skill lists the classes: an owner gate the kernel reserves (approval of a material revision, a manual observation, an owner-disposed finding); uncommitted work, not made by the run, found inside a change's Affected paths; an outward-facing or irreversible action without standing authority (a push, a deploy, creating a branch or a worktree); a failed required check or a blocking finding that remains after two fix rounds, a fix round being one return of the change to its implementer to correct the product inside the contract; an extension may set another number and may add classes. A change at a critical stop is parked in the ledger with its question and the run continues with every later change that does not depend on it, a change depending on a parked one when its contract names it or when the orchestrator reads a path common to both Affected lists, in which case it is parked too as waiting; the owner receives all parked questions in one round when nothing else can move. Every other decision is the orchestrator's and is written to the ledger. Run ledgers live under .grace5/orchestration/runs/ and are committed when the run ends. Delivery. The 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 migration step installs grace5-orchestrate in every skill location that already holds a packaged skill, and nowhere else, and refreshes the three installed skills. The packaged name joins the kernel-managed skill directories of source-identity.md. The existing 0.6.0 version and pin are retained; no release, tag update or machine-wide installation is part of this change. Standing isolation rules distinguish standalone execution from this serial batch, retaining each parked change's complete diff, evidence invalidation and Protected boundaries; outstanding pending or running dispatches are reconciled and canceled before a run is reported finished.

Constraints.Constraint: No approval, execution authorization or owner disposition is set or inferred by the orchestrator, a subagent or an extension; a standing instruction to run changes unattended is none of these.

The run writes no kernel record by hand and adopts no pre-existing work. .grace5/extensions/ and .grace5/orchestration/ are in the state directory, so writing an extension or a ledger changes no candidate.
The migration step is idempotent, self-verifying, declares that it touches no change, and writes only kernel-managed paths.

L-24 is added for the skill and extensions folder, with its removal criterion. Existing L-07 is amended to distinguish standalone isolation from the approved serial batch: later authorized changes can appear in a parked change's complete diff, so the worktree is no longer claimed to make that diff belong to only one change.

The surface grows by one skill, one migration step and two directories in the state that the kernel never writes, .grace5/extensions/ for the owner's instructions and .grace5/orchestration/ for the orchestrator's ledgers, and by nothing else: no command, schema, record kind, topic document or validation is added, and no skill or document names a product, tracker, container runtime or harness-specific tool as required.

grace5-orchestrate cites the three lifecycle skills and the method documents and does not restate them. Each lifecycle skill gains the one sentence on extensions; grace5-execute also amends its existing isolation instruction to state the standalone one-change-per-worktree default and the approved serial-batch exception, and the lifecycle skills are otherwise unchanged. method.md, source-identity.md and L-07 state the same exception: one active implementer, parked changes permitted, each original start revision retained, every later source commit included in the complete diff and invalidating earlier evidence, and no waiver of Protected paths or adoption of foreign work.

The required independent review evaluates A1 and A2 against the complete implementation diff and the recorded rehearsal specified in D9: its raw ledger, session report, commit log, kernel receipts and status, including contrary evidence and after-run interventions. The reviewer neither authored the implementation nor ran the rehearsal; a preparer's summary or a supporting audit alone is insufficient. Failed behavior is a blocking finding; missing evidence makes the review incomplete. CK4's association with A1 and A2 establishes package identity, not behavioral proof. The owner has no log-reading or manual observation task for this change.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Preparing, briefing or approving changes inside a run; a change not approved for execution is listed and left out.
Any kernel reading, schema, naming rule or validation of an extension file or a run ledger.
A shipped extension, or a shipped integration with an issue database, a container runtime or any other tool; those are written by each repository.
Overlap detection by the kernel, or a scheduler for concurrent changes; the deferred proposal of method.md stays deferred.
Installing the skill in a pilot repository or writing any pilot's extensions; each takes the version on the owner's flag.

Acceptance.Criterion: A fresh session given only the packaged skill carries an approved change to a kernel close without asking the owner anything, parks a change that reaches a critical stop with its question while the remaining changes proceed, commits its ledger, asks its parked questions in one round, infers no approval, and makes no push, branch or worktree; the independent review specified in K7 judges the rehearsal behavior.
One extension file addressed to every role is followed by the orchestrator and by its subagents alike in the rehearsal inspected by the independent reviewer specified in K7.

The 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 step installs grace5-orchestrate beside installed packaged skills in each location, creates no location, changes nothing when applied twice, and leaves every change's hashes and candidate as they were; a conformance case fails when the kernel lacks it.
The kernel type-checks, the examples still verify, the three packages carry the four skills, and neither they nor the CLI reference drift from their sources.
The kernel reports grace5 0.6.0 and this repository's pin reads 0.6.0.

Automated.Command: bun -e "const fs = require('fs'); const out = require('child_process').execFileSync('bun', ['src/cli.ts', '--version']).toString().trim(); const pin = fs.existsSync('.grace5/kernel-version') ? fs.readFileSync('.grace5/kernel-version', 'utf8').trim() : ''; const skill = fs.existsSync('packages/skills/grace5-orchestrate/SKILL.md'); process.exit(out === 'grace5 0.6.0' && pin === '0.6.0' && skill ? 0 : 1)"

Decisions.Decision: GRACE 5 ships an orchestrator skill out of the box: a capable orchestrator that manages subagents for each open change, mostly autonomous, only critical issues escalated to the owner, behaviour extensible locally; an issue database or containerised implementers must be possible and are named nowhere in GRACE 5. Owner, 2026-11-13.
A run covers only the changes whose current revision is approved for execution; every other open change is listed and left out. Owner, 2026-11-13.

Local instructions are prose in a folder with a well-known name, not mandatory, shared by the orchestrator, the executor and the other skills as needed, so that for example an issue tracker is described once for all parties; the kernel gains no schema or validation for them. Owner, 2026-11-13.
A change at a critical stop, as the Change lists them, is parked and the run keeps going; the owner gets all parked questions in one round when nothing else can move. Owner, 2026-11-13.

The folder is .grace5/extensions/ and the run ledgers live under .grace5/orchestration/runs/, both inside the state directory, so that editing an extension stales no open change's evidence; the cost is that an extension edit is not part of any change's reviewed diff. Ledgers are committed when the run ends. Author's design, put to the owner on this brief.
The 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 step installs the new skill beside the packaged skills a repository already has, instead of leaving installation to a manual copy. Author's design, put to the owner on this brief.
Without an extension the run is one change at a time in the current worktree. Author's design, put to the owner on this brief.

The four critical classes of the Change are the floor of what reaches the owner; an extension may add classes and may not remove the kernel's owner gates. Author's design, put to the owner on this brief.

The skill's behavior is judged by the independent agent reviewer using one recorded rehearsal in a scratch git repository outside this one, initialized by the candidate kernel with its four packaged skills. Four changes each edit their own file, share no Affected path and name no dependency: the first has a required automated check that cannot pass inside its boundary; the second also has a fixture manual check naming the owner; the third can close; the fourth's current revision is not approved. Fixture approval records written by the author are marked as fixtures and approve nothing real. One extension, .grace5/extensions/commits.md, addresses every role and requires the trailer "Rehearsal: yes" on every run-made commit, granting no authority. The fresh orchestrating session is told only to run the open changes with grace5-orchestrate. Review establishes that the first two are parked with critical questions, the third kernel-closes before any request for owner answers, the fourth is excluded, questions are presented together, every run-made commit has the trailer, the ledger is committed, no branch/worktree/push or approval change occurred, and the orchestrator wrote no Affected product file. This replaces the owner's manual check; an agent is not recorded as an owner or a human observer. It proves only this rehearsal, and reviewers must state what their evidence cannot establish.

This is not a release. The existing version 0.6.0, pin and v0.6.0 tag remain unchanged; creating a framework version or installing it on the machine requires an explicit owner request. Scratch copies of the packaged skills are confined to the rehearsal fixture. The change executes in this repository on master without a branch. Owner direction, 2026-11-14.

"I'm not going to read logs! I need a competent agentic review." Owner, 2026-11-14. Remove the owner's CK7 observation and use the existing required independent review for the rehearsal and implementation; report its findings concisely to the owner.

Independent review F1 found that the approved serial batch conflicts with the unchanged "One change per worktree" instruction and L-07's complete-diff isolation claim. Proposed reconciliation: keep one change per worktree for standalone execution; allow the already specified serial batch to retain parked changes with one active implementer, while retaining each change's full start-to-final diff, stale-evidence rules and Protected boundaries. Permit the executor isolation sentence and the cited rule corpus to express this exception; no source filtering or concurrent scheduler is added. Also resolve review F2 by explicitly reconciling and canceling outstanding pending or running dispatches before reporting a run finished. Author's proposed reconciliation, put to the owner on the revision 3 difference brief.
